interactables.label: To the visitor
interactables.title: To the visitor
interactables.text:
My name is Iona Vale. I tried to draw a final plan of this museum. The plan became so exact that it left no room for an exit.

I am still here, making corrections. Follow the numbered exhibitions. Bring each index weight to its matching plinth. Learn what a doorway actually promises.

When you have understood the building, please leave a way out for both of us.

interactables.label: An unfinished plan
interactables.title: An unfinished plan
interactables.text:
Ten exhibitions restore ten index plates. Each plate illuminates another doorway in this court.

J opens your notebook and exhibition map. H offers a hint, one step at a time. If a weight is misplaced, use Recall weight in the notebook. R returns you safely to the current exhibition entrance. Your discoveries are retained.

interactables.label: Accession 000
interactables.title: Accession 000
interactables.text:
A key, exhibited without a lock.

“Before we collected rooms, we collected the things that made rooms possible.”

interactables.label: Two norths
interactables.title: Two norths
interactables.text: The glass is continuous. The room is not. Follow the bronze frames, and carry the index weight back to the plinth.

interactables.label: All points north
interactables.title: All points north
interactables.text:
Four compasses, all labelled NORTH.

“The plan was accurate. Its paper was the problem.” — I.V.

interactables.label: The inside exceeds the outside
interactables.title: The inside exceeds the outside
interactables.text: The west collection holds the weight. The east collection holds its plinth. The archive’s glass partition has no opening. Both collections belong to this little pavilion.

interactables.label: A request for more drawers
interactables.title: A request for more drawers
interactables.text:
June: interior enlarged.
July: interior enlarged.
August: exterior dimensions unchanged.

No planning permission was required for the additional inside.

interactables.label: Everything that crosses
interactables.title: Everything that crosses
interactables.text:
Carry the weight into the measuring frame. Measure is shared by the visitor and the things they carry.

A quarter-size weight belongs beyond the low cabinet lip. The inverse passage restores your size.

interactables.label: Life size
interactables.title: Life size
interactables.text:
An enormous pencil and a miniature tea service. Both catalogue cards read: LIFE SIZE.

“I stopped calling one size the real one.” — I.V.

interactables.label: A settled arrangement
interactables.title: A settled arrangement
interactables.text:
Winter keeps the weight; summer holds its plinth.

Use the brass stand to release the current arrangement. While the arch stays in view it cannot move. Turn your whole view away for a moment, then look back.

interactables.label: Maintenance log
interactables.title: Maintenance log
interactables.text:
Watered the plants that were present.

“I thought I was being watched. I was the one preventing change.” — I.V.

interactables.label: One useful viewpoint
interactables.title: One useful viewpoint
interactables.text:
Stand on the ivory rings. Let the scattered frames become a single outline. Hold that view for one quiet breath.

A discovered connection remains available. You are free to look around after it settles.

interactables.label: Here
interactables.title: Here
interactables.text:
A sculptor tried to represent every view of a doorway at once. The result had no opening.

“A perspective is useful. It need not be universal.” — I.V.

interactables.label: The other floor
interactables.title: The other floor
interactables.text:
The right-hand wall is another gallery floor. The compass changes the direction in which you fall.

After you settle, W still walks forward; A and D walk across the new floor. The high north arch leads to the index plate. A second compass is mounted beside it for your return.

interactables.label: Premature labels
interactables.title: Premature labels
interactables.text: The chair was not attached to the wall. The chair was standing on a floor we had not yet agreed to use.

interactables.label: A route without a fixed scale
interactables.title: A route without a fixed scale
interactables.text:
The measuring arch halves all that passes. Its reverse doubles. The blue return preserves measure.

The little collection accepts one quarter of the starting weight. Find a route whose two halves do not undo one another.

interactables.label: Same place
interactables.title: Same place
interactables.text:
A visitor’s route: HALF → UNMEASURED → HALF → UNMEASURED.

At the bottom: “Same place. Different person.”

interactables.label: The same arch, another agreement
interactables.title: The same arch, another agreement
interactables.text:
The collection keeps a full weight. Conservation needs a half measure.

Release the arrangement, give it a moment outside your view, and the same frame takes on another destination — and another measure.

interactables.label: A correction
interactables.title: A correction
interactables.text:
TRAPPED is struck out.

“Connected to the wrong side.”

Below it, in a steadier hand: “I am alive. I can see the sky. Please finish the route.”

interactables.label: The unreachable viewpoint
interactables.title: The unreachable viewpoint
interactables.text: Take the weight. Turn the wall into a floor, and the ivory observation mark becomes somewhere you can stand. From there, the scattered frames admit a route.

interactables.label: The three corrections
interactables.title: The three corrections
interactables.text:
The last plan has three corrections:

OPEN — a room may be larger than its enclosure. Carry a half measure into its index.
HOLD — attention holds an arrangement. Release it to reach the other floor.
RELEASE — take that floor’s viewpoint. A complete outline admits the sky.

There is no combination to guess. Only a route to understand.

interactables.label: Three corrections
interactables.title: Three corrections
interactables.text:
OPEN — A half measure, carried through an impossible interior.
HOLD — Release the arrangement from your attention.
RELEASE — A view from the other floor.

You have already learned every part of this route. There is no secret sequence. Follow the named exhibitions.

interactables.label: Iona Vale, outside
interactables.title: Iona Vale, outside
interactables.text:
I am safely outside. The door held. I have left the gate open for you.

I thought that preserving this museum meant finishing its plan. You have shown me that a building can remain unfinished and still make room for someone.

The second cup is yours.
— Iona Vale

chapters.title: The Gallery of Two Norths
chapters.objective: Bring the weight behind the glass to the entrance plinth.
hints: A doorway promises a destination. It does not promise a direction.
The weight is behind the glass. The east arch and the arch beyond it reach the other side.
Enter the arch on the right, then the far arch in the long gallery. Take the weight behind the glass. Retrace both arches and place it on the entrance plinth.
chapters.reflection: A plan can be accurate and still fail to fit on paper.

chapters.title: The Small Pavilion
chapters.objective: Move the archive weight from the west collection to the east plinth.
hints: The exterior of a room does not determine its interior.
The two pavilion doors lead to opposite sides of the archive’s glass wall.
Enter the pavilion’s front door, take the weight on the west side, and return outside. Walk around the little pavilion and enter its rear door. Place the weight on the east plinth.
chapters.reflection: Storage exceeded the building. We retained the building.

chapters.title: The Scale Cabinet
chapters.objective: Carry a quarter-size weight through the low cabinet opening.
hints: The measure applies to everything that crosses with you.
Take the weight through the measuring arch. Your body, reach and weight become one quarter of their former size.
Pick up the weight beside the plinth, enter the 1:4 measuring arch, and walk under the low cabinet lip ahead. Place the tiny weight on the tiny plinth. Reverse the arch to become full size again.
chapters.reflection: I stopped calling one size the real one.

chapters.title: The Unseen Garden
chapters.objective: Carry the winter weight into the summer conservatory.
hints: An observed arrangement remains settled.
Release the arrangement at the brass stand, then turn fully away from the arch. It changes only while you are not looking.
Enter WINTER and take its weight. Return, use Release the arrangement, and face the entrance until the latch sounds. Turn back and enter SUMMER. Fill its plinth.
chapters.reflection: I was the one preventing change.

chapters.title: The Sightline
chapters.objective: Complete the broken outline and retrieve its index weight.
hints: Separate frames can share a single outline.
Stand on the ivory observation mark and look through the bronze frames. Hold the view until the connection settles.

Stand inside the marked ring near the entrance. Aim at the centre of the far bronze frame and hold for a moment. The doorway stays open. Cross it, take the weight, return and fill the entrance plinth.
chapters.reflection: A perspective is useful. It need not be universal.

chapters.title: The Gravity Atrium
chapters.objective: Reach the high gallery by walking on its other floor.
hints: Floor describes an agreement, not a material.
The compass makes the east wall down. The high arch then becomes a doorway at walking height.

Use Change the floor. Let yourself settle on the right wall. Move along that wall to the elevated north arch, at height seven on the old wall. Cross to the record gallery and take the index plate. Use the wall compass after returning to restore the floor.
chapters.reflection: An object is not falling wrongly. We labelled the room prematurely.

chapters.title: The Hall of Measures
chapters.objective: Choose a route that makes the weight one quarter without undoing it.
hints: You can return to a place without returning to your former measure.
The blue UNMEASURED arch keeps your size. Two trips through the half-size arch make a quarter.

Carry the weight through 1:2. Return through UNMEASURED, not through 2:1. Repeat this loop once. At quarter size, enter the little cabinet on the left and fill its plinth. Reverse the measuring route twice to grow back, or use entrance recovery.

chapters.title: Blind Transit
chapters.objective: Reach the conservation side with the correctly measured weight.
hints: The arrangement selects both a destination and a measure.
COLLECTION holds a full weight. CONSERVATION measures everything to one half.
Take the weight from COLLECTION and return. Release the arrangement and turn away. Enter the newly revealed 1:2 CONSERVATION route while carrying the weight. Place the half-size weight on its plinth.
chapters.reflection: Not trapped. Connected to the wrong side.

chapters.title: The Ceiling Observatory
chapters.objective: Reach the wall viewpoint and carry its weight into the record room.
hints: Some viewpoints have to be reached before they can be understood.
The observation mark is on the other floor. Change gravity and walk to it.

Take the weight, use the compass, then walk on the east wall to the ivory mark at old height six, near the centre. Aim at the high north frame until it opens. Carry the weight through and fill the record-room plinth.
chapters.reflection: I can see the outside. I need a route that admits it.

chapters.title: Exit Without Exterior
chapters.objective: Complete OPEN, HOLD and RELEASE to make a route into the morning.
hints: The unfinished plan asks for an interior, a measure, an arrangement and a viewpoint you already understand.
OPEN: take the weight inside the little pavilion, then through its half-measure passage. HOLD: release the arrangement after filling OPEN. RELEASE: reach the other floor’s viewpoint.

Enter the pavilion, take its weight, carry it through 1:2 and fill OPEN. Use 2:1 RETURN to restore your size. Release the main arrangement and look away. Enter HOLD, use its compass, reach the wall’s ivory mark and align the far frame. Walk through RELEASE into the courtyard, then sign the ledger.
chapters.reflection: A way out is something we make possible for one another.
